lore: At the harbour mouth stands a tall gauge post marked in fathoms. Gauge-keeper Corwin drops his lead line beside every island and reads how much water it needs under its keel to stay green, to stay off the rocks, and for the whole world to ride at anchor together. Then he looks at tonight's tide and calls the harbour deep, shoal, or aground.

lines.deep: Deep water under every keel. Every lamp green, every island at anchor.
lines.shoal: We float, but a few keels are scraping. A little more water and the lamps go green.
lines.aground: Aground. The tide is lower than the gauge mark; raise the budget or lighten the islands.
